name: Maize
fact: Ghana's most widely grown cereal and the base of kenkey, banku and TZ.

name: Local Rice
fact: Home-grown 'Ghana rice' is rising in demand against imports.

name: Millet
fact: A drought-hardy grain used for porridge and 'koko' in the north.

name: Sorghum
fact: Used for pito brewing, tuo zaafi and porridge.

name: Cassava
fact: Processed into gari, fufu and agbelima; harvest within 48 hours.

name: Yam
fact: Pona yam from Techiman is famous across West Africa.

name: Cocoyam
fact: Corms and leaves are used for fufu and kontomire stew.

name: Sweet Potato
fact: Orange-fleshed types are rich in vitamin A.

name: Plantain
fact: Eaten fried as kelewele, boiled, or with ampesi.

name: Pineapple
fact: Ghana's MD2 pineapples are exported to Europe.

name: Tomatoes
fact: The base of nearly every Ghanaian stew; very perishable.

name: Pepper
fact: Shito, kpakpo shito and scotch bonnet are everyday staples.

name: Onions
fact: Cured onions from Bolgatanga and Tamale store for months.

name: Okra
fact: Used for okro soup, a favourite across the country.

name: Garden Egg
fact: Eaten in stews and agushie, and as a snack with groundnuts.

name: Groundnut
fact: Used for groundnut soup, paste and roasted snacks.

name: Cowpea
fact: Beans for waakye and red-red, rich in protein.

name: Soybean
fact: A growing cash crop for poultry feed and oil.

name: Cocoa
fact: Ghana is one of the world's top two cocoa producers.

name: Cashew
fact: Raw nuts are exported mainly to Vietnam and India.

name: Oil Palm
fact: Source of palm oil for abenkwan and local cooking.
